summary: Covers z/OS tips for raw, copy/fetch and blockinfile/lineinfile. raw ignores the remote environment so you prefix export statements, copy and fetch don't keep tags so you re-tag with chtag, and line-editing modules need UTF-8 files that you re-tag afterwards.
questions: How do I use the raw module on z/OS UNIX?
Does copy keep the file tag when copying to z/OS?
Can I use lineinfile on an EBCDIC file on z/OS?
Which environment variables does raw need on z/OS?
How do I restore a file tag after fetch or copy?

answer_card.title: raw, copy, fetch and lineinfile on z/OS
answer_card.answer_md:
- **raw** ignores remote environment settings, so export the minimum variables before your command:

```yaml
ansible.builtin.raw: |
        export _BPXK_AUTOCVT: "ON" ;
        export _CEE_RUNOPTS: "FILETAG(AUTOCVT,AUTOTAG) POSIX(ON)" ;
        export _TAG_REDIR_ERR: "txt" ;
        export _TAG_REDIR_IN: "txt" ;
        export _TAG_REDIR_OUT: "txt" ;
        echo "hello world!"
```

  Or use `command`/`shell`, which apply the configured remote environment.
- **copy / fetch** don't tag files and don't keep existing tags. Copying as binary is safe, but re-tag afterwards:

```yaml
- name: Tag my_file.txt as UTF-8.
  ansible.builtin.command: chtag -tc iso8859-1 my_file.txt
```
- **blockinfile / lineinfile** process data as UTF-8. Make sure files are UTF-8 first and re-tag them afterwards.
